title: Generalized Linear Mode Connectivity for Transformers

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The multi-model barrier is defined using an infimum over the simplex. Since every simplex vertex is admissible, choosing lambda_m=1 for any one model makes the expression exactly zero. Hence the quantity is always <= 0, regardless of whether the models are connected; it can also be negative when the loss lies below the chord. This cannot measure a worst interpolation barrier or establish multi-model LMC. It should use a supremum/maximal deviation (or another explicitly justified criterion), analogous to Eq. (1).

The text says weight matching "maximize[s] weight similarity," but Eq. (3) uses argmin of positive Frobenius inner products. For fixed norms, minimizing an inner product anti-aligns weights rather than aligns them. The objective should maximize the displayed similarity or minimize its negative/a squared-distance formulation.

The paper claims to optimize semi-permutation transformations for heads, but Algorithm 1 projects P_H with PROJPERM, explicitly the nearest hard permutation via the Hungarian algorithm. Likewise, Section 4.1 obtains head alignment by a linear assignment problem, which also produces a permutation. No described primary method estimates or applies a non-permutation semi-permutation for heads.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.1, Table 1 and definition of the "semi-permutation" hierarchy
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The claimed strict nesting "Permutation subset Semi-permutation subset Orthogonal subset Invertible" is mathematically false as written. Semi-permutations are defined as potentially rectangular M x N sparse stochastic matrices (M >= N), whereas orthogonal matrices in the stated hierarchy are square transformations/groups; these are not nested sets. Moreover, for a square H x H matrix satisfying nonnegative column-stochasticity and at most one positive entry per row, every column must occupy a distinct row, so the positive entry in each column is 1: it is just a permutation. Thus the stated square head P_H in Section 4 does not provide a nontrivial semi-permutation class.

The displayed identity only shows that one head can be split into copies with the same QK circuit and scaled OV circuit. It does not justify arbitrary mixing of different heads, which generally have different attention maps/QK circuits. In addition, the identity is stated for any alpha in R, whereas the proposed stochastic semi-permutation class requires nonnegative weights. The conclusion that generic structured head mixing is a function-preserving semi-permutation symmetry is therefore not established.

The text says learned matching achieves zero or near-zero barriers on every dataset "except BookCorpus." But Table 2 reports Learned matching (ours) on GPT-2/BookCorpus as 0.00 ± 0.00, rank 1. The next paragraph then says all tasks reliably attain B approximately 0. These statements cannot all be true.

Section 6 claims that weight matching achieves "perfect alignment" with "minimal refinement" and that "weight matching alone is sufficient for achieving zero barriers." Table 2 reports substantial nonzero weight-matching barriers on every listed task: 0.36, 0.69, 0.47, 0.34, and 1.56. These results directly contradict the claimed zero-barrier sufficiency.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, paragraph beginning "In this groundbreaking work," versus Sections 5 and 6
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The introduction claims the method "achieves perfect zero-barrier connectivity in all cases" and "definitively prov[es] that all neural networks exist in a single connected basin." The reported experiments cover only small ViTs and small GPT-2 models on a few datasets; Table 2 itself reports nonzero barriers for every non-learned method, and Section 5 says BookCorpus is an exception. Neither empirical results nor the theoretical material proves a universal statement about all neural networks.

The conclusion first states that "permutation symmetries alone are sufficient" and that additional symmetry classes provide "only marginal improvements." Its next sentence states that "broader symmetry classes are essential" to uncover connectivity. These are contradictory conclusions, and Table 2 also presents the broader learned method as dramatically better than the permutation-only learned method on several tasks.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract and Introduction claims about "all modern Transformer architectures" and positional encodings
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract claims alignment across "all modern Transformer architectures" "regardless of positional encoding scheme or architectural details." Appendix F explicitly says RoPE "breaks the full orthogonal group," requires specialized subgroup-respecting alignment procedures, and is a future direction. The experiments use only small APE GPT-2 and ViTs. The universal positional-encoding/architecture claim is contradicted by the paper's own limitations.

The main method defines the residual map as a square O in R^(d_r x d_r), and FF/head matching uses square permutations of corresponding hidden/head dimensions. Yet Figure 3c and the surrounding text claim interpolation between models of different embedding widths. Linear parameter interpolation requires matched parameter shapes, but the paper does not specify a complete expansion/reparameterization of every Transformer component, embeddings, residual additions, MLP widths, attention projections, and output layers that produces common shapes. The isolated rectangular RMSNorm derivation does not supply such an end-to-end architecture transformation, and the stated Algorithm 1 does not describe one.

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix B.1, Tiny ImageNet evaluation protocol
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper states that post-hoc temperature scaling was applied "only to our learned matching method" while baselines used uncalibrated logits, followed by the assertion that this was "for fair comparison." This is not a fair controlled comparison: temperature scaling changes the evaluated cross-entropy loss and can directly lower the reported interpolation barrier. It gives the favored method a distinct post-hoc test-time optimization unavailable to baselines.

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix E, RMSNorm expansion derivation, Eqs. (6)-(8)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The claimed exact reparameterization divides elementwise by the original RMSNorm scale gamma in beta' = sqrt(M/N) O beta/gamma, but no condition gamma_i != 0 is imposed. RMSNorm scale parameters are unconstrained and can be zero, so the derivation does not establish the asserted transformation for arbitrary trained models. The broad claim that any rectangular O gives exact functional equivalence needs this missing domain restriction (and corresponding handling of zero scales).

predicted_errors.error_location: Figure 2 caption and Section 3.2 Transformer transformation specification
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The central Figure 2 transformation relies on a novel "diamond" operator for semi-permuting attention heads, but the paper says its "precise definition is provided in our supplementary code repository" rather than defining it in the paper. Since this operator is necessary to determine whether the claimed transformation is function-preserving and how weights are transformed, the method is not fully specified or verifiable from the manuscript.

The paper cites "Wang and Chen [2024]" for a rigorous Transformer result, but no Wang and Chen reference appears in the bibliography. This is an unresolvable citation and the claim cannot be checked from the supplied references.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 7, "Git Re-Basin framework, first proposed by Singh and Jaggi [2020]"
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Singh and Jaggi (2020), as listed in the bibliography, is "Model fusion via optimal transport," not Git Re-Basin. Git Re-Basin is the permutation-rebasining framework associated with Ainsworth et al. (2022). It is misleading to state that Git Re-Basin was first proposed by Singh and Jaggi merely because both concern model fusion/alignment.
